questions.q: How much heat does a linear BEC dissipate with a 25 V input, a 5 V output and a 0.5 A current?
questions.explain: (25 − 5) V × 0.5 A = 10 W: a linear regulator dumps the whole voltage difference as heat.

questions.q: Why a low-ESR capacitor on the power bus?
options: To absorb spikes from the inductance
To protect the battery connector from reverse polarity
questions.explain: U = L·dI/dt during ESC switching: the capacitor acts as a local source and clips the spikes.

questions.q: What voltage margin should the capacitor have on 6S (25.2 V full charge)?
questions.explain: 30 % (32.8 V) is only the minimum; braking spikes on 6S exceed 35 V, so 50 V (1.98 × full charge); 35 V is for 4S.

options: A fuse in series with the motor wires
questions.explain: A bulb or resistor in series with the positive at the first power-up after soldering: on a short the bulb lights up and the aircraft does not smoke.

questions.q: Why is voltage sag dangerous for the FC?
questions.explain: Buck converters have a minimum input voltage; sag below it restarts the board.

questions.q: What happens to a connector overloaded with current?
options: It reduces ripple on the power bus
questions.explain: Heating → oxidation → higher resistance → even more heating.

questions.q: Which BEC is best for powering the receiver and the sensitive RF part?
questions.explain: An LDO produces no ripple; a buck → LDO chain gives both efficiency and a clean supply.

questions.q: A Raspberry Pi on board reboots during maneuvers. In dmesg:
questions.fragment:
[  812.4] hwmon hwmon1: Undervoltage detected!
[  812.9] hwmon hwmon1: Voltage normalised
Power: 5 V / 1 A BEC from the flight controller
options: A 1 A BEC cannot power the Pi (up to 2–3 A): sag on the peaks, so you need a separate 5 V / 5 A BEC
CPU overheating: hwmon reports throttling, not voltage
The memory card is damaged and the kernel misreads write errors as sag
The message is normal: the Pi always logs it when Wi-Fi starts, and it can be ignored
questions.explain: The Pi reports the sag itself; the onboard 5 V from the FC is meant for light loads.
